thread:
Maya (support): Customer SUP-12345 reports intermittent 500s from Android app behind corporate proxy. No request-id visible in their logs or response headers. Happens ~2026-03-15 14:12 UTC.
Ava (eng): Could be header stripping at the proxy. Ask for a curl from a workstation outside the proxy or a HAR/mitm capture from the device. Short checklist and a one-liner will help.
Maya (support): Asked for HAR / curl. They replied with app logs only and say they can't enable debug in prod yet. Sending our suggested steps.
Ravi (eng): Minimal repro/capture steps to send the support team — paste this to the customer: 

1) curl (captures response headers):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate |& tee curl-out.txt
# then: grep -i "request-id" curl-out.txt || true
```

2) Browser: DevTools -> Network -> right-click -> Save all as HAR. Attach har file.

3) Android (if app): use mitmproxy/Charles on a laptop, install device cert, capture the request. Export as HAR or mitm dump.

4) If none of the above show a request id, provide: exact client timestamp (UTC), public client IP, user-agent string, and the raw curl-out.txt or pcap. We can correlate on ingress logs.

Also ask infra to check their proxy logs for outbound requests to api.redwood.ai around the timestamp (proxy may rewrite or drop x-request-id).

Maya (support): Sent that. Customer asked for exact SDK debug flag names (Android/iOS).
Ava (eng): SDK notes (common):
- Android SDK: enable client debug logging with `ClientConfig.debug = true` or call `client.enableDebugging(true)` before the request. This will print request/response headers and the internal request id to logcat.
- iOS SDK: set `RDWClient.shared.debug = YES` or run with the verbose flag in the app.
If they cannot change the app binary, they must do a proxy capture.

Ravi (eng): If proxy is involved, common header names we add: `X-Request-Id` (our primary), `x-redwood-request-id` (fallback), and `traceparent` for W3C tracing. Ask their infra to preserve those when forwarding.

Maya (support): Customer says their proxy 'CorpEdge' rewrites headers. They will ask infra to search for outbound requests at 2026-03-15T14:12:00Z ±2min and return any matching X-Request-Id values.

Ravi (eng): If they can't provide the header, we can still try: please ask for the following in the debug bundle — all files attached to the ticket: `curl-out.txt` (from step 1), `har.zip` (browser/mitm export), `sdk-verbose.log` (if they can enable it), proxy logs (if allowed), and the exact request timestamps (UTC) and public IP. With that we can search our ingress logs by IP+minute and find the internal request id and full trace.

Tom (sre): If they provide pcap/pcapng, we can extract the TCP stream around the timestamp and parse HTTP headers; add a note that pcap may contain secrets — have them redact keys or provide a short-lived key for repro. I'm taking this onto the correlation queue. :white_check_mark: 

Maya (support): Customer is producing a HAR and the curl output now. I told them to redact the auth token and keep the headers intact.

Ava (eng): Quick grep for us when we get the HAR: `jq -r '.log.entries[].request.headers[] | select(.name|ascii_downcase=="x-request-id") | .value' har.json || true` — also search for `traceparent` and `x-redwood-request-id`.

Maya (support): Perfect. I'll attach everything to SUP-12345 and ping eng once uploaded. Thanks all :thumbsup:
